description_full: PTC Inc. operates as software company in the Americas, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. The company provides Windchill, a suite that manages all aspects of the product development lifecycle(PLM) that provides real-time information sharing, dynamic data visualization, collaborate across geographically distributed teams, and enabling manufacturers to elevate product development, manufacturing, field service, and end-of-life processes; ServiceMax, a service lifecycle management solutions enable companies to asset uptime with optimized in-person and remote service and technician productivity with mobile tools, and deliver metrics; and Arena, a SaaS PLM solution enables product teams to collaborate virtually to share product and quality information with internal teams and supply chain partners and deliver products to customers. It offers Codebeamer, an application lifecycle management for products and software development; Servigistics, a service parts management solution; and FlexPLM, a platform for merchandising and line planning, materials management, sampling, and others. In addition, it offers Creo, a 3D CAD technology enables the digital design, testing, and modification of product models; and Onshape, a SaaS product development platform that delivers computer-aided design with data management, collaboration tools, and real-time analytics. Further, it offers Vuforia, an augmented reality (AR) software; and Arbortext, a dynamic publishing solution streamlines how organizations create, manage, and publish technical documentation. Additionally, the company provides PTC Products; PTC Mathcad; and augmented reality product. PTC Inc. was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts.

financial_summary: PTC Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $21.5B market cap on $2.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years and +9% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 74% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $873M in free cash flow — roughly 32 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.87× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 7.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 33% operating margin runs 26pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 11% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 0% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 48% and a beta of 0.93, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $298.9M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 45% in the 2020 crash, 21% in the 2022 bear market and 66% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $68.90 (margin of safety -186%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 24%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $29.86 to $147 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: EV/EBITDA 22.1 vs 16.6 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 40% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 14 covering analysts target $202 on average, 2% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 11% earns above the cost of capital of 8.9%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.67).
It runs a 74% gross margin and converts 32% of revenue into free cash flow, or 23% after stock compensation.
ROE of 30% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 14pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 17.6% of revenue on R&D and 9.2% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.4x net debt to EBITDA ($232.9M of cash against $1.6B of debt), with interest covered 12.8x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.4, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 51% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.2% over 3 years, 8.6% over 5 years and 9.1% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 3% of profits supports about 0.3% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 20.5% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.95 and a backlog worth 1.0x annual revenue.
Capex runs only 0.3x depreciation (0.9% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.4%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 7.5% a year to shareholders (7.5% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 7,305 employees, each generates about $374K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and revenue has grown 6.4% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $119K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.6M (7x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
